source_text: Age iam, qui voles curiositatem melius exercere in negotio salutis tuae, percurre ecclesias apostolicas, apud quas ipsae adhuc cathedrae apostolorum suis locis praesident, apud quas ipsae authenticae litterae eorum recitantur, sonantes vocem et repraesentantes faciem uniuscuiusque. Proxima est tibi Achaia, habes Corinthum. Si non longe es a Macedonia, habes Philippos, habes Thessalonicenses. Si potes in Asiam tendere, habes Ephesum. Si autem Italiae adiaces, habes Romam, unde nobis quoque auctoritas praesto est. Ista quam felix ecclesia cui totam doctrinam apostoli cum sanguine suo profuderunt, ubi Petrus passioni dominicae adaequatur, ubi Paulus Ioannis exitu coronatur, ubi apostolus Ioannes, posteaquam in oleum igneum demersus nibil passus est, in insulam relegatur. Videamus quid didicerit, quid docuerit, cum Africanis quoque ecclesiis contesserarit. Unum deum dominum novit, creatorem universitatis, et Christum Iesum ex virgine Maria filium dei creatoris, et carnis resurrectionem; legem et prophetas cum evangelicis et apostolicis litteris miscet; inde potat fidem; eam aqua signat, sancto spiritu vestit, eucharistia pascit, martyrium exhortatur, et ita adversus hanc institutionem neminem recipit. Haec est institutio, non dico iam, quae futuras haereses praenuntiabat, sed de qua haereses prodierunt. Sed non sunt ex illa ex quo factae sunt adversus illam. Etiam de olivae nucleo mitis et opimae et necessariae asper oleaster oritur, etiam de papavere ficus gratissimae et suavissimae ventosa et vana caprificus exsurgit. Ita et haereses de nostro frutice, non nostro genere, veritatis grano, sed mendacio silvestres.
thought_title: The apostolic churches as the living proof of the rule of faith
orientation: Tertullian is addressing a Christian who wants to exercise curiosity about salvation, telling him to visit the apostolic churches where the apostles' own chairs and authentic letters still remain.
pass_a_gloss: Come now, you who wish to exercise curiosity better in the matter of your salvation, run through the apostolic churches, among which the very chairs of the apostles still preside in their own places, among which the very authentic letters of theirs are read aloud, sounding the voice and representing the face of each one. Achaia is nearest to you; you have Corinth. If you are not far from Macedonia, you have Philippi, you have the Thessalonians. If you can make your way into Asia, you have Ephesus. But if you lie near Italy, you have Rome, from which authority is also at hand for us. How happy is that church on which the apostles poured out their whole teaching with their own blood, where Peter is made equal to the Lord's passion, where Paul is crowned with John's departure, where the apostle John, after he was plunged into fiery oil and suffered nothing, is banished to an island. Let us see what he learned, what he taught, when he also entered into fellowship with the African churches. He knows one God as Lord, the creator of the universe, and Christ Jesus from the virgin Mary, the Son of God the creator, and the resurrection of the flesh; he mingles the law and the prophets with the evangelical and apostolic writings; from there he drinks faith; he signs it with water, clothes it with the Holy Spirit, feeds it with the Eucharist, exhorts it to martyrdom, and so against this institution he receives no one. This is the institution, I do not say now, which was foretelling future heresies, but from which heresies came forth. But they are not from it from the time when they were made against it. Even from the seed of the mild and rich and necessary olive the wild and bitter oleaster arises; even from the fig seed of the most pleasing and sweet fig the windy and empty wild fig springs up. So also heresies arise from our stock, not of our kind, from the grain of truth, but wild through falsehood.

choices.why: Keeps the literal force of 'exercere' (to exercise, practice) and 'melius' (better), preserving Tertullian's ironic concession to the seeker's desire for curiosity.
Renders 'authenticae' literally as 'authentic' to convey the original documents written by the apostles themselves, not copies.

choices.english: is made equal to the Lord's passion
choices.why: Preserves the passive force of 'adaequatur' and the literal 'dominicae' (of the Lord), showing Peter's death as matching Christ's suffering.
rejected: suffers a death like the Lord's
is matched to the Lord's passion

choices.why: Keeps the ablative of means 'exitu' (departure, death) and the metaphor of crowning, which Tertullian uses for martyrdom.
rejected: receives the crown of John's death

choices.why: Renders 'igneum' as 'fiery' and 'demersus' as 'plunged into', preserving the vivid physical detail of the attempted execution.
Keeps the literal 'nibil' (nothing) and 'passus est' (suffered), emphasizing the miraculous preservation of John.

pass_b_english: Come now, if you want to exercise your curiosity more profitably in the business of your salvation, travel through the apostolic churches, where the very chairs of the apostles still preside in their places, where their authentic letters are read aloud, sounding their voice and making each one's face present. Achaia is near you, so you have Corinth. If you are not far from Macedonia, you have Philippi and the Thessalonians. If you can make your way to Asia, you have Ephesus. If you are close to Italy, you have Rome, from which authority is also available to us.

How happy is that church, on which the apostles poured out their whole teaching with their own blood, where Peter is made equal to the Lord's passion, where Paul is crowned with John's departure, where the apostle John, after being cast into a cauldron of boiling oil and suffering nothing, is banished to an island. Let us see what he learned and what he taught, since he also entered into fellowship with the African churches. He acknowledges one God, the Lord, the creator of the universe, and Christ Jesus born of the virgin Mary, the Son of the creator God, and the resurrection of the flesh. He mingles the law and the prophets with the evangelical and apostolic writings; from these he drinks faith; he signs it with water, clothes it with the Holy Spirit, feeds it with the Eucharist, urges it to martyrdom, and so he receives no one against this institution.

This is the institution—I do not say now the one that was foretelling future heresies, but the one from which heresies came forth. But they are not from it, since they were made against it. Even from the pit of the mild, rich, and necessary olive, the wild oleaster springs up; even from the poppy, the windy and empty wild fig rises from the most pleasing and sweet figs. So also heresies come from our shrub, but not of our kind—from the grain of truth, but wild with falsehood.

problems.why: 'Nations' and 'Gentiles' alternate for the same concept without explanation.
problems.fix: Use one term consistently or note at first occurrence that they are synonymous.

problems.quote: where the apostle John, after being plunged into fiery oil
problems.why: This refers to the tradition of John being boiled in oil, but 'plunged into fiery oil' is an odd rendering.
problems.fix: Use 'cast into a cauldron of boiling oil' or similar.

edits.old: after being plunged into fiery oil
edits.new: after being cast into a cauldron of boiling oil

fixed: The glossary note about 'the nations' is not a problem in this section: the English does not use 'the nations' or 'Gentiles' here, so no edit is needed.

The source 'in oleum igneum demersus' describes John being plunged into fiery oil; the English 'plunged into fiery oil' is a literal but odd rendering. Changed to 'cast into a cauldron of boiling oil' to convey the traditional account naturally.
